title: Complete Hierarchy of Nonrelativistic Odd-Parity Spin Splitting in Collinear Magnets
authors: Yichen Liu, Junxi Yu, Pu Zhang, Cheng-Cheng Liu
abstract: Momentum-dependent nonrelativistic spin splitting provides a symmetry fingerprint of collinear magnets and can govern unconventional electronic, magnonic, and transport phenomena. Whereas even-parity $s$-, $d$-, $g$-, and $i$-wave splittings in collinear magnets have been extensively studied, odd-parity counterparts remain unexplored beyond the $p$-wave and $f$-wave classes. Here, using group theory, we establish the complete classification of odd-parity spin splitting in collinear magnets. We show that, in addition to the $p$-wave and $f$-wave forms, $h$- and $k$-wave splittings with $\ell=5$ and $7$ are allowed, while $m$-wave splitting with $\ell=9$ constitutes the upper bound. We derive a complete mapping from crystallographic point-group irreducible representations to the lowest-order odd-parity basis functions and formulate the coupling rule between a symmetry-breaking axial field and the parent Néel order that selects the induced odd-parity class. We further construct minimal lattice models that realize $h$-, $k$-, and $m$-wave splitting. Guided by this classification, we screen the MAGNDATA database and show that circularly polarized light can drive the $\mathcal{PT}$-symmetric antiferromagnets Fe$_2$TeO$_6$ and MgFe$_6$Ge$_6$ into $h$-wave and $k$-wave phases, respectively, exhibiting the hallmark spin splittings in both electronic bands and magnon spectra. Symmetry analysis and Berry-curvature calculations show that collinear odd-parity magnets of both $h$- and $k$-wave allow an anomalous Hall response, whereas the $m$-wave class forbids it. Together, these results complete the partial-wave hierarchy of odd-parity spin splitting in collinear magnets and establish symmetry criteria for anomalous transport in the high-partial-wave classes.
summary: This work establishes a comprehensive, symmetry-based classification scheme for nonrelativistic odd-parity spin splitting in collinear magnets, extending the known partial-wave hierarchy up to $\ell=9$. By mapping crystal symmetries to allowed spin-splitting forms, the authors predict which high-partial-wave classes can exhibit anomalous Hall responses, providing crucial diagnostic tools for experimental condensed matter physics.
main_problem: To establish a complete symmetry classification of nonrelativistic odd-parity spin splitting ($\Delta E(k)$) in collinear magnets, extending beyond known $p$- and $f$-wave classes.
main_result: A complete hierarchy is established showing allowed odd-parity classes up to $\ell=9$ ($m$-wave), providing symmetry criteria for anomalous transport; specific materials like Fe2TeO6 realize h-wave splitting.
method: The authors use group theory, applying a two-step classification procedure involving the parent Néel order and an axial field to determine allowed spin-splitting representations ($\Gamma_{\Delta}$).
model_or_system: The study focuses on collinear magnets, modeled using minimal symmetry-adapted four-band tight-binding Hamiltonians. The splitting is induced by breaking effective time-reversal symmetry, often simulated via Floquet driving.
key_observables: Odd-parity spin splitting $\Delta E(k)$, anomalous Hall conductivity ($\sigma_{xy}$), and characteristic features in electronic/magnon spectra for different wave classes.
important_parameters: Partial-wave order $\ell$ (ranging from 1 to 9); the symmetry point group of the magnet; coupling strength of the axial field.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes collinear magnetic ordering and relies on specific symmetry breaking mechanisms, such as Floquet driving by circularly polarized light.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the complete hierarchy (p, f, h, k, m waves) and show spin-resolved electronic/magnon spectra for realized materials under light-induced phases. Figure 4 shows calculated anomalous Hall conductivity.
paper_structure: The paper systematically develops a group-theoretical framework using Tables I and II to classify $\Gamma_{\Delta}$, constructs minimal lattice models for $h$-, $k$-, and $m$-waves, applies this classification to known materials (Fe2TeO6, MgFe6Ge6), and finally uses the symmetry constraints to predict anomalous transport properties.
why_interesting: The rigorous application of group theory to classify momentum-dependent spin splittings provides powerful predictive tools for understanding exotic magnetotransport phenomena in quantum materials.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Complete hierarchy of nonrelativistic odd-parity spin splitting in collinear magnets. The surfaces visualize the angular dependence of the partial-wave form factor of ∆E(k) = E↑(k)−E↓(k), with red and blue denoting positive and negative signs. The upper row shows the p-wave basis z and representative f-wave bases xyz and y(3x2 −y2); the lower row shows the h-, k-, and m-wave bases xyz(x2 −y2), xyz(3x2 −y2)(3y2 −x2), and xyz(x2 −y2)(y2 −z2)(x2 −z2).

FIG. 2. Minimal symmetry-adapted models for high-partial- wave odd-parity spin splitting. Panels (a)-(c) show the spin- resolved band structures of the h-, k-, and m-wave models, respectively, with red and blue denoting the spin-up and spin- down sectors. Panels (d)-(f) show the corresponding isoen- ergy surfaces at E = −3t in the cubic, hexagonal, and cubic Brillouin zones, respectively; the colors distinguish the two spin channels. In each model, the nearest-neighbor hopping amplitude t is taken as the energy unit. The parameters are J = t, λh = 0.2t, λk = 0.5t, and λm = 0.1t.
